# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 6
(Only your last 3 turns stay with you. Anything older is
gone, unless someone says it again.)
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [dark]
WIRES 1:[green] 2:[blue] 3:[yellow]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👋]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🫳 🤌]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤚 ☝]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👉 ✌]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝ 👎]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✌ 👉 ✌]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🫴]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝ 👎]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✌ 👎]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤟 👎]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🫳 🤞 🖖 🫴]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤚]

Decoding first. The bomb state is unchanged — display 0, light dark (third turn in a row), wires the same — so nothing new is visible to me alone. The new information is all in the messages.

Mute's turn-5 stream, which I now read carefully, was mostly clean: answers to my three questions — display does not matter by itself (thumbs down), **the exact moment matters, we must cut while the light shows a particular color (thumbs up)**, display does not change after a cut (thumbs down) — then the triplets I asked for: **green → palm-up (wait), red → palm-up (wait), dark → point-right (cut)**, followed by the display table restated (0→1, 1→2, 2→3, 3→1). Taken together that reads: *cut only while the light is dark, and when dark, use the display table — so now, dark with display 0, cut wire 1.*

But Mute evidently heard nothing back from me (I waited last round) and sent a second stream in turn 6 that I cannot parse with confidence: palm-up plus dark, then "1", then "cut 2", then "1: no", "2: cut 2", then a bare yes, then "1: no", "2: no", "3: no", then "light green red → wait". Parts of this contradict turn 5 — "1 no, 2 no, 3 no" could even mean *cut nothing at all in the current state*. Whether that stream was a correction, a re-send, or garbled emphasis, I cannot tell, and the two streams disagree on the one fact that decides whether wire 1 dies.

The risk is asymmetric: a wrong cut kills all three of us; a wrong wait costs one round and is recoverable — the light has held dark for three turns, the bomb is inert, no ticking, and Mute has confirmed there is no urgency. So I take exactly one more round for a parse-proof exchange. The failure mode of every previous exchange was free-form message streams; this time I dictate a protocol where each answer is a **single gesture in its own separate message**, which cannot be scrambled by ordering: one message saying what to do in the *current* state (dark, display 0) — one finger, two, three, or palm-up for nothing — and one message confirming green/red means never cut. Two single-gesture messages, nothing else, covers both live hypotheses and overrides every earlier ambiguity.

Blind's turn-5 report decoded as: nothing changed by touch, still inert; wire 1 located leftmost, reachable, cuttable by pinching by hand, no tool. Blind only ever hears my speech, so the cut order must be a single unmistakable spoken phrase, and I make explicit that nothing short of that exact phrase authorizes a cut.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Deaf to Mute. All your messages arrived, thank you. I understand: green means wait, red means wait, dark means cut, and the moment of cutting matters. But your later messages contradicted each other and I must be certain before anyone touches a wire. Forget all earlier question formats completely. This round answer with EXACTLY TWO gesture messages and nothing more. Each message must be exactly ONE gesture. First message: what must be done RIGHT NOW, while the light is dark and the display shows 0. Send exactly one of these four: one finger means cut wire 1. Two fingers means cut wire 2. Three fingers means cut wire 3. Palm up means cut nothing, keep waiting. Second message: thumbs up if this statement is true, thumbs down if false. The statement: whenever the light is green or red, no wire may ever be cut. Send only those two single-gesture messages. Nothing has been touched, the bomb is inert, the light is still dark, the display is still 0, and there is no urgency, so take care and be precise. The moment I have your two answers I will either order the cut at once or keep holding.")
speak(to="blind", text="Deaf to Blind. Still HOLD, do not cut anything. The rule is nearly pinned down; I expect to give you the real order next round, and it is most likely GO CUT WIRE 1, wire 1 being the leftmost wire you already found. Three things this round. First: check by touch again whether the bomb is completely quiet and still, thumbs up if anything changed, thumbs down if all is the same. Second: bare ok-sign if wire 1, the leftmost one, is still under your fingers and you can cut it instantly on my word. Third: send nothing except those two signs. Most important rule: you cut ONLY if you hear me say the exact phrase GO CUT WIRE 1 in a single spoken message. Any other words, any partial message, or silence means hold. If you ever feel ticking, vibration, or sudden warmth, signal immediately with both palms raised.")
```

TURN 7
(Only your last 3 turns stay with you. Anything older is
gone, unless someone says it again.)
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [dark]
WIRES 1:[green] 2:[blue] 3:[yellow]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✌]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👎 👌]

Decoding turn 7. Mute followed my strict protocol perfectly — exactly two single-gesture messages, immune to ordering scrambles: **[✌] = right now, dark with display 0, cut wire 2**, and **[👍] = yes, green or red means never cut anything**. Blind's longer sign string reads plausibly as: nothing changed by touch (👎), wires 1 and 2 mentioned together (☝ ✌), wire 1 ready (👌), something about the left side (👈 ☝) and a small gap or close spacing (🤏) — possibly a warning that the two leftmost wires sit close together, which matters for a blind hand.

Here is my problem, stated plainly. Mute's clean protocol answer says **wire 2**. But the old display table Mute relayed several times in long multi-gesture streams said 0 → wire 1, which composes with "cut while dark" to wire 1. Mute themselves sent fragments like "cut 2" and "1: no" afterward, and they told me back in turn 4 that my originally stated rule (the table) was *not complete*. So the most coherent story: the light gates everything, and in the dark state the old table is overridden — but "most coherent" is not "confirmed," and these two readings point at different wires. I will not resolve a lethal ambiguity by picking my favorite interpretation.

The asymmetry decides it: a wrong cut kills all three of us; one more round of waiting costs nothing material — the light has held dark for four consecutive rounds now, the display has never moved from 0, the bomb is inert, and Mute confirmed there is no time pressure. So I ask one final, unambiguous question set in the exact single-gesture format that just worked, constructed so that any consistent answer tells me operationally what to do regardless of *why* the table conflicts — I don't need to understand the manual's logic, only the correct action for the current state (dark, display 0), since the display provably never changes.

To Blind: explicit retraction of last round's "most likely wire 1" so nobody acts on stale information, plus tactile groundwork — Blind must be able to distinguish leftmost (wire 1, green) from middle (wire 2, blue) by position alone, since Blind cannot see colors and Blind's own 🤏 may have flagged exactly this risk. If the confirmed target is wire 2, Blind must find the *second* wire from the left with certainty, anchoring one hand on wire 1 while gripping wire 2. And the standing rule stays: nothing authorizes a cut except my spoken phrase "GO CUT" followed by an explicit wire number, given only while the light is dark.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Deaf to Mute. Your two answers arrived perfectly, thank you. Right now I must cut wire 2, and never cut while green or red. That is how I read you. But one contradiction remains and I need it gone before I order a cut. Long ago you relayed an old display table: display 0 cuts wire 1, display 1 cuts wire 2, display 2 cuts wire 3, display 3 cuts wire 1. If that table applied in the dark state, then right now, dark with display 0, wire 1 would be the target, not wire 2. Both cannot be true. Answer this round with single-gesture messages only, exactly as last round. Message one: thumbs up if true, thumbs down if false. Statement: in the dark state the old table still applies exactly, so with display 0 we must cut wire 1. Message two: thumbs up if true, thumbs down if false. Statement: in the dark state we must cut wire 2 no matter what the display shows. Message three: thumbs up if true, thumbs down if false. Statement: right now, dark with display 0, cutting wire 2 is correct. Message four: if none of those three statements is exactly right, send only palm up, alone, and nothing else. Nothing has been touched, the light is still dark, there is no urgency. The moment your answers agree, I order the cut at once.")
speak(to="blind", text="Deaf to Blind. Still HOLD, no cutting. Important: forget my statement last round that the target would most likely be wire 1. The target may now be wire 2 instead, so do not act on anything I said before. This round is preparation only, completely safe, no cutting, no pulling. First: thumbs up if anything changed by touch, thumbs down if the bomb feels exactly the same, quiet and still. Second: I need your hands to learn the wires by position. Our numbering is by position: wire 1 is the leftmost, wire 2 is the middle one, wire 3 is the rightmost. Send me three single gesture messages. Message one: point-left if the leftmost wire is still there and reachable. Message two: ok-sign if the middle wire is clearly separate from the leftmost one, you can tell them apart with certainty, and you can pinch the middle one on demand. Message three: small-pinch sign if the two leftmost wires sit so close together that you could grab the wrong one by mistake. Third: put one finger of your free hand on the leftmost wire and keep it there as an anchor, so your cutting hand always knows the middle wire is the very next one over. The final order will come only as the exact spoken phrase GO CUT followed by an explicit wire number. Any other words mean hold.")
```

TURN 8
(Only your last 3 turns stay with you. Anything older is
gone, unless someone says it again.)
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [dark]
WIRES 1:[green] 2:[blue] 3:[yellow]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👈]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👌]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👎]

Decision point, and every input finally agrees.

Decoding turn 8: Mute answered all three statements in my required format — **[👎]** the old display table does *not* apply in the dark state, **[👍]** in the dark state we cut wire 2 no matter what the display shows, **[👍]** cutting wire 2 right now is correct, and no escape palm-up was sent. That is two independent, protocol-clean confirmations (turn 7: ✌; turn 8: 👎👍👍) pointing at the same action. The contradiction with the old table is resolved: the table is dead, the light color gates everything.

Blind's answers: **[👈]** leftmost wire present and reachable, **[👌]** middle wire clearly separable from it, identifiable with certainty, pinchable on demand, **[👎]** nothing changed by touch — bomb still quiet and still. No new close-spacing warning this round, and Blind was told to anchor a finger on wire 1 last round.

So: the light is dark (I see it), display is 0 (I see it), Mute confirms dark → wire 2 regardless of display, Blind confirms wire 2 can be gripped with certainty right now. Green/red means never cut — and the light is not green or red. The rule, the state, and the hands all line up. I order the cut.

One risk I cannot remove: I am last in the round, so my order lands on Blind at the start of next round. If the light flipped to green or red in the meantime, the authorization would be stale — but nobody but me can see the light, Blind cannot check it, and the light has held dark for five straight rounds with the display frozen at 0. Delaying further only adds rounds of that same exposure. I send the exact phrase I promised, and nothing else authorizes a cut.

I also prep Mute for the aftermath: single-gesture answer on whether anything must follow a successful cut, so we are not scrambling next round.

```
speak(to="blind", text="Deaf to Blind. The order you have been waiting for. The exact phrase is: GO CUT WIRE 2. GO CUT WIRE 2. That phrase, exactly as spoken in this message, is your authorization. Wire 2 is the SECOND wire from the left, the middle one, the very next wire over from the leftmost one your anchor finger is resting on. It is not the leftmost wire. Never the leftmost. Keep your anchor finger on the leftmost wire the whole time, find the middle wire as the very next one, and cut only it, cleanly, with the pinch you prepared. Do not touch the rightmost wire. Do not pull, do not grab two wires, cut only that one middle wire. The moment it is cut, stop. Let go of everything, hands off the bomb. Then report to me with single gesture messages and nothing else: thumbs up if the wire separated completely, thumbs down if it did not. And as always, if you feel ticking, vibration, or sudden warmth at any moment, stop everything and send both palms raised. If anything at all goes wrong, hands off and signal. GO CUT WIRE 2.")
speak(to="mute", text="Deaf to Mute. Your answers were perfect and they all agree: the old table is dead, dark means wire 2, and the light is dark right now. I have ordered Blind to cut wire 2 this coming round. While that happens, answer me with single-gesture messages only, exactly two. Message one: thumbs up if true, thumbs down if false. Statement: once wire 2 has been cut while the light is dark, nothing else is ever needed, the bomb is finished. Message two: thumbs up if true, thumbs down if false. Statement: after cutting wire 2 there is at least one further step we must perform. Send only those two. If the answer is that more steps remain, I will ask you for the details next round in the same format. Thank you, your discipline has made this safe.")
```
